subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration, SDK changes & function-calling fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@acme-corp.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration, SDK changes & function-calling fit

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of needs / pain points (as we heard them)
- High-throughput customer message enrichment pipeline (low latency for streaming chat)
- Need structured outputs for downstream routing (JSON objects with intent, metadata)
- Reranking/embeddings for search and recommendation quality improvements
- Tight security/compliance constraints (data residency + audit logs)

Product & integration fit we discussed
- SDK changes: you will likely use our Python SDK v1.8 with the new streaming client (supports incremental token frames + on_chunk hooks). We called out a small shim to adapt your existing websocket consumer.
- Function calling: Redwood's function-calling schema maps well to your intent-to-action step; we showed how a single model response can surface a structured call (action name + typed args) that your orchestrator can execute.
- Streaming & structured outputs: streaming + structured outputs together let you render partial UI updates while guaranteeing eventual valid JSON. We flagged the tools around our structured type validators.
- Embeddings & reranking: we recommended a two-step hybrid approach  embeddings for semantic recall (document retrieval) + model-based reranking for precision.

Open items / technical clarifications
1) Bandwidth / concurrency targets  you mentioned ~300 concurrent users with 95th pct response < 400ms. We flagged that Dedicated or a reserved pool will be the right fit.
2) Data residency  you need EU-only storage for logs for a subset of traffic; we can map that to a Dedicated region or Private deployment.
3) SDK migration delta  we estimated ~2-3 engineer-weeks for the websocket shim + function-call wiring.

Next steps
- Marissa / Dylan: share the integration MVP plan + sample Postman collection (attached). (Action: marissa_cole)  by Fri 3/12
- Acme: confirm PII scoping and expected retention window so we can propose retention config (Action: Alex / Priya)  by Mon 3/15
- Technical call (SE deep-dive)  propose Tue 3/16 10am PT (well send invite)

Attachments: redwood-integration-mvp-plan.pdf, function-calling-sample.postman, sdk-migration-notes.md

Thanks  happy to iterate on the plan.

fa
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration, SDK changes & function-calling fit

Thanks Marissa  this is great and captures the convo. A few clarifications from our side:

- Concurrency/latency: 300 concurrent is an average target; burst to ~800 for marketing events is possible. 95th pct ideally < 300ms for text completions; for streaming chat partial rendering we can tolerate slightly higher.
- Structured outputs: we need the JSON schema to include a confidence score per field (so our router can fallback). Can your function-calling model include confidence metadata?
- Reranking: we favor embeddings for initial recall. We'll want to run a short A/B to compare reranker variations (model-based vs lightweight logistic reranker).

We're comfortable with a 2–3 week engineering lift for the proof-of-concept, assuming we can get a mock dataset and the Postman collection. I'll confirm PII scoping with Priya and come back with specifics.

Good to tentatively lock in the SE deep-dive on Tue 3/16 10am PT.

faAlex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

Hi Alex / team 

Following up with technical notes from our SE side after reviewing the mock data you shared on the call: 

SDK & integration notes\- Python SDK v1.8 has a StreamingClient that emits token chunks and an on_chunk callback. To keep your existing websocket consumer we recommend a lightweight adapter that:
  1) opens a single connection per user session
  2) forwards token frames to your websocket backend as they arrive
  3) handles reconnect logic with Redwood's resume token headers

Function calling & structured outputs\- Our function-calling output includes a metadata stanza we can populate with per-field confidence (we call it field_confidence). We can deliver a sample schema in the SE call.

Embeddings & reranking\- We'll deliver a small notebook that builds FAISS indexes from embeddings and a sample reranking pipeline (model-score + cosine). For the POC, recommend: 1M doc sample downsampled to 50k for initial perf testing.

Security / data residency\- For EU-only logs we can scope audit logs to your dedicated region; for the POC we can keep test data in us-west until we finalize controls.

Action items (technical)
- Dev: share StreamingClient adapter example + sample schema for function-calling with field_confidence (attached sdk-migration-notes.md).  by Thu 3/11 EOD
- Acme: share a representative mock dataset (50k docs or smaller) and list of fields that need confidence scores  Alex / Priya  by Mon 3/15

I'll attach the quick Postman and sample notebook in the follow-up message.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
